title: Why JavaScript logs in a surprising order
subtitle: The event loop explains callbacks, timers, and promises
learning_objective: Explain why synchronous code runs before queued callbacks and promise reactions.

scenes.title: GUESS THE OUTPUT
scenes.body: A log runs, a timer is scheduled, and a Promise resolves. The order is not the order you wrote them in.

scenes.title: Finish the current job first
scenes.body: JavaScript runs the current synchronous stack to completion. Promise reactions are queued as microtasks; timer callbacks run later as tasks when eligible.

scenes.title: Predict this
Why it matters
scenes.body: A zero-millisecond timer does not interrupt current code. Avoid using timers as a guarantee that another operation has finished.

scenes.question: What is the output order?
scenes.explanation: Both synchronous logs run first. Promise reactions run before the timer callback in this example.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Synchronous stack first, then queued microtasks, then eligible tasks such as timers.
